explanation: Remember the last position of each word. The nearest earlier equal word is always its latest occurrence, so checking those distances suffices. Return −1 if no repeated word is found.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: For the current word, any earlier occurrence farther left than its latest occurrence gives a no-smaller distance. Therefore checking only the stored latest index is sufficient at every position. The minimum across those nearest predecessor distances is the global nearest repetition.
walkthrough: In ["sun","rain","wind","sun","rain"], sun repeats at indices 0 and 3 and rain at indices 1 and 4. Both distances are 3, so return 3.
edgeCases: Return −1 when every word is distinct.
A word occurring many times must update its latest index after every occurrence.
